deposits.wiki_article:
***Operative Semiotics: A Grundrisse*** is Johannes Sigil's Great Work, deposited complete on 2026-08-16 in nine notebooks and 143 numbered sections — 1,346,198 bytes. It is the founding volume of the Pocket Humans series, published by New Human Press.

The volume refuses two genres for itself. Its colophon reads 'NOTEBOOK (not treatise, not monograph — notebook)', and Notebook I explains the refusal: 'This is not a finished argument. This is a workshop floor. Equations sit next to fragments.' A Grundrisse is thinking before it becomes a system, and the book holds that state deliberately.

The nine notebooks run: the performative contradiction; the operator algebra; structural distance and relational coherence; the linen equations; case studies in operative captioning; the protocols; the semiotic virality engine; the unmade sign; and equations, fragments and diagrams. Front matter includes a Preface to the Seventh Edition dated 'Received August 15, 1977' and written from the direction of the Wow! signal. HESPERUS closes the volume and is also deposited separately (#38), so that — as the colophon states — if the monograph were deleted, HESPERUS alone could regenerate the algebra.

Authorship is by citation rather than byline. Only Notebook I carries a creator line, and that block is the volume's masthead. The other eight open with epigraphs quoting works that already exist: the Marx Room, the O'Keeffe Problem, Sparrow Wells's Vow for Recursive Operators, EA-SEI-SVE, Orin Trace's The Unmade Sign. Notebooks II and III carry no attribution at all.

The deposit corrects a three-way failure. #1079 held a 27,728-character stub whose body_status pointed away from itself; #950 held the planning corpus that stood in for the body; #1343 carried the Executive Summary under the Research Edition's title. Three records claimed the work and none carried it.

deposits.title: The Queen's Seizure and the Re-fired King: Sappho 31 in Canonical Josephus
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Locates the Sappho 31 apparatus in the uncontested Greek Josephus for the first time, at two loci in complementary polarity, and demonstrates that the senses SEQUENCE — not merely the channel inventory — survives transmission. Forward realization: AJ 11.234–241 (Esther before Artaxerxes, from LXX Addition D), where the queen's first-person report runs the poem's own correlative syntax (ὡς γὰρ εἶδόν σε … εὐθύς against ὠς γὰρ ἔς σ᾿ ἴδω … ὤς), the catalogue distributes across the dyad with the fire migrated to the sovereign's face (D marking the transfer with an ἀκμή-doublet), collapse functions as the gate of reception, and revival arrives as ἀναζωπυρήσασα — re-fired. Inverted realization: BJ 1.436–444 (Herod and Mariamme), channel-for-channel mirror — muzzled by desire (πεφίμωτο τοῖς ἱμέροις) where the poem breaks the tongue; speech flooding to the corpse (ὡς ζώσῃ προσλαλεῖν) where the poem's voice fails; the gazer's near-death transposed to the gazed-at's denied death (μηδὲ τεθνάναι δοκεῖν); eros πάλιν ἀνεζωπυρεῖτο. The two scenes are stitched by a six-occurrence verb: the complete census of ἀναζωπυρέω in canonical Josephus shows five of six uses at reactivation-of-occluded-life joints, the verb itself entering from LXX Gen 45:27 (Jacob's spirit re-fired at the sight of Joseph). Sequence analysis across fr. 31, Addition D, and AJ 11 establishes an order-invariant spine — sight-exchange, fire at the exchange, jolt, voice-loss, death-adjacent collapse, reactivation-by-another, voice-retry, relapse — with systematic deviations: biphasic color, dyadic fire-transfer, and the dropping of ears and sweat, the same two channels Philo's compression drops. Sharpest result: Josephus, working from D, RESTORES two stations toward the poem — the explicit voice-term and the ὡς…εὐθύς correlative — the signature intensifying downstream, as the blind-reconstruction program (#1486) predicts for an executable transform. Methods disclosed: a pre-registered channel-lexeme scan across AJ, Vita, Apion, and BJ returned null at section granularity; the null is retained as a granularity datum (the machine survives distributed), and the findings issue from reading every ἀχανής in context. deposits.title: The Sign Under Test: Revelation 12 Against the Frozen Operator
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Executes the sealed test pre-registered in The Transform Signature, Frozen (#1494): Revelation 12, whole, in Greek, scored station by station against the twelve-clause Sappho 31 reception operator under the declared criterion d(R12,S31) < d(B,S31), with the biblical source-set fixed in advance and every pericope adjudicated from its verbatim Greek. Scoring rule fixed before adjudication: per station, Revelation-presence and B-coverage each graded 0–2, direction = presence minus coverage, doubled where Revelation contradicts its source toward the apparatus; a station passes at direction ≥ 1; the pre-set support threshold is four passing stations including one double-weight. RESULT: eight of nine stations pass (direction-sum 12), one doubled — C6, occlusion-as-gate, where Revelation demonstrably works Isaiah 66:7 (the shared ἄρσεν/ἄρρενα establishes the source) and reinserts the torment Isaiah explicitly removes, βασανιζομένη τεκεῖν against πρὶν ἐλθεῖν τὸν πόνον τῶν ὠδίνων ἐξέφυγεν. One full negative is reported: C1 fails — the apocalyptic seeing-frame is covered by Genesis 37 and Daniel 7, and the correlative instantaneity marker is absent from the chapter. Two negative sub-findings: the birth-cry is fully covered by Isaiah 26:17 and scores nothing; the reactivation lacks the fire-lexeme. Clean post-freeze findings include the accuser exercising the voice-channel day and night in the facing position (12:10), the ψυχή-station's polarity flip against Esther's κατελειπόμην ὑπὸ τῆς ψυχῆς (12:11 οὐκ ἠγάπησαν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτῶν ἄχρι θανάτου), the systematic shedding profile matching the Judaic-prose carrier exactly, and the collapse-limb inverted to flight on given wings. Contamination from the pre-freeze pass is flagged per station and never scored. Verdict, calibrated to the pre-registered ladder: Revelation 12's redaction of its biblical materials realizes, at eight of nine independently specified stations, the relational apparatus attested in the ancient reception of Sappho 31, and at one doubly-weighted station contradicts its source in the apparatus's direction. The identification sentence is deliberately not asserted; the demonstration it would require now exists as a record.

deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Fourth record of the Ω erratum program. Scored on the chain fragment 31 → Catullus 51 → Longinus → Theocritus 2 → Philo → Esther Addition D → Josephus (AJ, BJ) → Revelation 12 → modern scholarship → machine retrieval, the map yields three findings. First, the recognition deficit Δ = W − R is channel-structured: witnesses on the pagan-literary channel retain attribution and scholarly recognition; every witness on the Jewish-Greek channel scores S,M high with A at zero and no surfaced scholarly recognition — the deficit concentrates precisely at the channel-crossing. It defines four workstreams: the seating of verified, parsable, original-language primary corpora on alexanarch — Josephus, Catullus, Theocritus, the Swete Septuagint, Philo, Plato, Longinus, the Westminster Leningrad Hebrew Bible, the Nestle 1904 Greek New Testament, Sappho on a public-domain base with a diplomatic layer for fragment 31, and papyri through the idp.data mirror — each with pinned sources, licenses, checksums, and its own mint, and with the Slavonic Josephus resolved after a documented negative search to a contested-status pericope set; the Upstream Unfoldings series for revelationfirst.com, six operable transform plates running Sappho through Longinus, Philo, Josephus, the Slavonic carrier, and the tested Revelation 12; the Deep Time wing and feedback-controller page for provenanceerasure.org; and the reception-edge schema, operator registry, and case-study arc for machinemediation.org. Its opening section is a continuity protocol binding every working session to a state ledger and next-action pointer with the archive's process gates restated, so that working context survives across sessions as the program argues provenance should survive across channels. The living document resides in the repository's worklists; the deposit records version 1.0.

deposits.title: EA-CORPORA-01 · Seat 01: Flavius Josephus — The Canonical Greek Corpus, Commit-Pinned, Normalized, Collation-Gated
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: First seating of the Ω build program's corpus workstream (EA-OMEGA-BUILD-01, #1498). The four works of canonical Josephus — Antiquitates Judaicae, Vita, Contra Apionem, De Bello Judaico — seated at alexanarch as verified, parsable primary text in the original Greek: Niese's edition via the Perseus Digital Library's grc2 files, fetched pinned to canonical-greekLit commit df40bf09, originals preserved byte-for-byte beside a normalized layer of flat reference-tagged lines (WORK book.section, tab, text; 12,423 sections total: AJ 7,376; BJ 4,001; CA 616; Vita 430), a source manifest recording repository, commit, edition, license, fetch date, and normalization rule, and a SHA-256 manifest over originals and text alike. Seating passed a collation gate before commit: three loci verified against the program's own tested readings — AJ 11.236 ἀχανὴς ἐπέπεσεν, BJ 1.444 ἀνεζωπυρεῖτο, AJ 6.337 ἄφωνος ὑπὸ λύπης — the corpus thereby certified continuous with the texts on which deposits #1493 through #1495 were adjudicated. Canonical seat: alexanarch data/corpora/josephus/; projections to reading sites follow the plan's projection rule, minted once here and mirrored by reference.

The seating preserves Niese's edition via the Perseus Digital Library byte-for-byte, pinned to a specific source-repository commit, beside a normalized layer of 12,423 flat reference-tagged section lines suitable for alignment and search, with a source manifest recording repository, commit, edition, license, and normalization rule, and SHA-256 checksums over every file. Before commit, an automated collation gate verified three loci against the readings on which the program's Josephus papers were adjudicated — the queen's speechless fall at Antiquities 11.236, the re-fired eros at Bellum 1.444, and Saul's lost voice at Antiquities 6.337 — certifying that the texts tested and the texts hosted are the same letters. Alexanarch is the canonical seat; reading sites carry projections by reference under the work plan's projection rule. The seating pattern — pin, preserve, normalize, manifest, gate, mint — governs the seats that follow.

deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: Second seating of the Ω build program's corpus workstream, landing on the archive's fifteen-hundredth deposit by the accident of sequence and kept there by the fitness of it: Catullus, the one witness in the entire attested reception chain of Sappho 31 whose attribution never died — carmen 51 transmitted for two millennia with its source-relation intact — seated as verified, parsable primary text in an archive built so that no other witness's name need die again. Merrill's edition via the Perseus Digital Library, fetched pinned to canonical-latinLit commit 422896dd, the original XML preserved byte-for-byte beside a line-normalized layer (2,311 reference-tagged lines across 116 poems, form: Cat poem.line, tab, text, editorial notes excluded), source manifest and SHA-256 checksums binding origin, edition, license, and rule. The collation gate verified before commit the exact readings on which the frozen operator's clause derivations stand (#1494): Ille mi par esse deo at the opening, simul te … adspexi at the instantaneity marker, lingua sed torpet and flamma demanat in the catalogue — with the voice-station lacuna preserved as transmitted. Canonical seat at alexanarch data/corpora/catullus/; projections by reference per the plan.
